### Season outlook as written in the guide (p. 238)

For the first time since 2016, the Rockets will not be playing for Jason Candle. Hell, for the first time since 2009, Candle isn’t even with the program. He’s now the head coach at UConn and the Rockets moved quickly to replace him with Mike Jacobs, who spent the last two seasons with Mercer at the FCS level. Jacobs is a northwest Ohio native and his staff also consists of people with Ohio ties, including former Tiffin and Ohio Dominican head coach OC Cris Reisert and Cleveland native and Youngstown State DC Jahmal Brown. Jacobs was a long snapper and offensive lineman at Ohio State from 1997-2001 and got into coaching pretty much right after that. His first head coaching gig was at Notre Dame College about a half hour from downtown Cleveland. This is something of a step up for the 47-year-old, but he took Mercer to the playoffs in back-to-back seasons and may very well be an upgrade over Candle, something hard to say about a guy who won 65% of his games overall and 68% of conference games. Over 7.5 The schedule is pretty soft for Jacobs in Year 1, as the Rockets don’t face Miami of Ohio, get reigning champ Western Michigan at home, and get a visit from San Diego State in non-conference action. It will take time for things to come together and the opener against Michigan State may not be pretty, especially for a defense that allowed just 13.3 PPG and 96 rushing yards per game last season, but Jacobs seems like a good hire and there’s at least some familiarity thanks to all the transfers from a team that finished in the FCS Top 25 each of the last two seasons. My projection is 8.04 wins.

## 26. Open Questions / Risks

The guide's *Three Burning Questions for the 2026 Season* *(p. 239)*, with the answers as written:

### Holy Toledo, who are these guys?

There are virtually no recognizable names on the roster for the Rockets this season. Returning production is hard to find, as the top returnee in tackles had 35 and the top returnee in yards of any kind had 194 receiving yards. It’s hardly a surprise, as Candle left when a lot of his players were running out of eligibility and a head coach leaving means that the transfer portal is wide open. 247Sports lists 37 transfers for the Rockets, who have the third-best MAC class per their ranking. John Alan Richter is not one of those transfers, so he’s a name that Rockets fans may recognize. Otherwise, there are a lot of Mercer transfers who were with Jacobs, including RB CJ Miller and WR Adjatay Dabbs, plus there are some faces on the OL familiar to Reisert, as they came with him from Gardner-Webb.

### What kind of offense should we expect to see?

Under Jacobs, Mercer racked up 6.8 yards per play last season with a balanced approach that left them third in the nation in yards per game. The Bears had 4.9 yards per carry on more than 400 rushing attempts and threw for over 3,800 yards. Toledo may have been a little more run-heavy last season, but that’s also because they had a lot of leads to protect and some big leads at that. Obviously this year’s team won’t have the same defense as last year’s squad, so we’ll have to wait and see how the game state plays out. With Miller, Penn State transfer Cory Smith, and two senior tackles who played for the Rockets last season, I would expect them to lean on the run at the outset.

### What kind of defense should we expect to see?

This is going to be an aggressive defense under Brown. Last year’s Mercer group only allowed 3.4 yards per carry, but gave up 5.7 yards per play because they got burned for some explosives in the passing game. The Bears had 42 sacks in 12 games, but also only generated 15 takeaways. With 96 tackles for loss, you can see how they pursued the run heavily and also got to the quarterback, but an evasive QB had the chance to burn them. There are some running QBs in the MAC, but not as many this season as we’ve seen in other years. With quite a few Mercer transfers who know the scheme, this should be an exciting defense to watch.
